title: Sporifica Virus
description: Simulate a virus carrier moving on an infinite grid with evolving infection rules.
writeup:
## Approach

The puzzle describes an infinite grid of nodes, each of which can be in different states depending on the part of the puzzle. A virus carrier moves through the grid, turning based on the state of the current node, updating that node's state, and then moving forward.

The grid is sparse, so the most efficient representation is a dictionary keyed by `(row, col)` coordinates. Any node not in the dictionary is implicitly clean.

Movement is tracked using `(dr, dc)` direction vectors, and turning is implemented by rotating these vectors left or right.

## Part 1

Nodes have only two states: clean and infected. The carrier:
- Turns left on clean nodes, right on infected nodes.
- Flips the node's state (clean → infected, infected → clean).
- Moves forward.

We simulate 10,000 bursts and count how many times a clean node becomes infected.

## Part 2

The virus evolves and nodes now have four states:
- Clean (.)
- Weakened (W)
- Infected (#)
- Flagged (F)

The carrier's behavior changes:
- Clean → turn left
- Weakened → do not turn
- Infected → turn right
- Flagged → reverse direction

State transitions follow:
Clean → Weakened → Infected → Flagged → Clean

We simulate 10 million bursts. The answer is how many times a node becomes infected.

This requires efficient dictionary operations and careful direction handling, but runs comfortably within time limits.
